deck.title: WAF, Shield & the Security Service Zoo
deck.analogy: Your application is a nightclub with a layered security crew: WAF is the bouncer reading IDs, Shield is riot police for mobs, Firewall Manager is head of security for the whole chain, and GuardDuty/Macie/Inspector are detectives watching the cameras.

subtopics.title: Firewall Manager — the head of security for the whole chain
The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: What layer does AWS WAF work at, and what can it read?

back.answer: Layer 7 (application layer); it reads HTTP requests: URLs, headers, query strings, body.
back.explanation: Layers 3/4 are raw IP packets and TCP connections; WAF sees the HTTP content a packet firewall cannot.
back.mnemonic: WAF = the smart bouncer who reads every ID.

cards.front: AWS WAF: what does a SQL injection rule catch?

back.answer: SQL injection such as ' OR 1=1 -- hidden in a form field.

cards.front: AWS WAF: what does an XSS rule catch?

back.answer: Cross-Site Scripting: malicious <script> tags in input.

cards.front: AWS WAF: what does a rate-based rule do?

back.answer: Blocks an IP that sends too many requests per IP in 5 minutes.

cards.front: AWS WAF: what do geo-match rules do?

back.answer: Block or allow requests by country.

cards.front: AWS WAF: what are IP sets?

back.answer: Explicit allow/deny lists of IP addresses.

cards.front: AWS WAF: what are managed rule groups?

back.answer: Pre-built rule packs from AWS/vendors, e.g. the OWASP Top 10 core rule set.

cards.front: AWS WAF keyword: **"rate limit requests per IP"**

back.answer: WAF rate-based rule
back.explanation: Too many requests per IP in 5 minutes blocks that IP.

cards.front: How do you test a new AWS WAF rule against production traffic without breaking real users?

back.answer: Use Count mode: the rule counts matches instead of blocking.
back.explanation: "Evaluate a new rule without impacting users" means Count mode.

cards.front: Which resources can AWS WAF attach to?

back.answer: CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito User Pools.

cards.front: Can you attach AWS WAF to a Network Load Balancer?

back.answer: No. NLB is Layer 4 (TCP) and never parses HTTP; WAF needs an L7 front.
back.explanation: WAF also cannot attach to EC2 directly or Route 53.

cards.front: What is a DDoS attack?

back.answer: Distributed Denial of Service: thousands of machines flood you with traffic to knock you offline.
back.mnemonic: Shield = riot police for the mob.

cards.front: What is AWS Shield Standard?

back.answer: Free, automatic DDoS protection for everyone, against common Layer 3/4 attacks (SYN floods, UDP reflection).

cards.front: What does AWS Shield Advanced cost and add?

back.answer: About $3,000/month (1-year commitment); adds L7 DDoS protection, 24/7 DRT, and cost protection.
back.explanation: Cost protection refunds scaling charges caused by the attack.

cards.front: Shield Standard vs Shield Advanced: which fits "L7 DDoS, expert help, refunds for attack-driven scaling"?

back.answer: Shield Advanced; plain "common DDoS at no cost" is Shield Standard (already on).

cards.front: What does AWS Firewall Manager do?

back.answer: Central policy manager: defines WAF, Shield Advanced, Security Group, Network Firewall policies once and auto-applies them across the Organization, including new accounts.
back.mnemonic: Head of security making every club follow the same door policy.

cards.sourceHeading: Firewall Manager — the head of security for the whole chain

cards.front: What are the prerequisites for AWS Firewall Manager?

back.answer: AWS Organizations and AWS Config enabled.

cards.sourceHeading: Firewall Manager — the head of security for the whole chain

cards.front: "Every new account automatically gets the security policies": WAF or Firewall Manager?

back.answer: Firewall Manager. WAF is the rule; Firewall Manager is the rollout machine.

cards.sourceHeading: Firewall Manager — the head of security for the whole chain

cards.front: What is AWS Network Firewall?

back.answer: A managed firewall for the whole VPC inspecting Layers 3–7: intrusion prevention, domain filtering, stateful rules.
back.explanation: Covers all traffic entering/leaving the VPC, not just HTTP to one ALB.

cards.front: Network Firewall keyword: **"filter outbound traffic to specific domains for the entire VPC"**

back.answer: Network Firewall

cards.front: What does Amazon GuardDuty do?

back.answer: Agentless ML threat detection on CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs; finds cryptomining, unusual API calls, compromised credentials.

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: What does Amazon Macie do?

back.answer: Discovers PII/sensitive data in S3 using ML (credit cards, SSNs).

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: What does Amazon Inspector do?

back.answer: Vulnerability scanner for CVEs on EC2 (via SSM agent), ECR container images, and Lambda.

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: What does AWS Security Hub do?

back.answer: Aggregation dashboard for findings from GuardDuty/Macie/Inspector etc., plus compliance standards (CIS, PCI).

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: What does Amazon Detective do?

back.answer: Investigates after a finding, building a relationship graph to find the root cause.

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: What is AWS Artifact?

back.answer: Download AWS compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO) to hand to auditors.

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: How do GuardDuty, Macie, Inspector, Security Hub and Detective relate in flow?

back.answer: GuardDuty/Macie/Inspector send findings to Security Hub; Detective finds the root cause afterwards.
back.mnemonic: Findings → one dashboard → "why did this happen?" → Detective.

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: GuardDuty vs Inspector: which is which?

back.answer: GuardDuty watches behavior in logs (threats now); Inspector scans software for vulnerabilities. Threat = GuardDuty; CVE = Inspector.

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: Can Macie scan EC2 or RDS for sensitive data?

back.answer: No. Macie is S3-only.

cards.sourceHeading: The detection zoo — one-liners you must know cold

cards.front: Block SQL injection attacks against an application behind an ALB. Which solution?

back.answer: WAF on the ALB.

choices.why: Covers L3/L4 DDoS, not SQL injection.
VPC-wide inspection, not the ALB SQLi answer.
Detects threats in logs, doesn't block.

cards.front: Limit each client IP to 2,000 requests per 5 minutes. Which solution?

back.answer: WAF rate-based rule.
back.explanation: Per-IP rate limit is WAF's signature move.

choices.why: DDoS protection, not per-IP rate limiting.
Distributes policies; doesn't rate limit itself.

cards.front: Protection against common DDoS attacks at no additional cost. Which solution?

back.answer: Shield Standard.

cards.front: After a large DDoS, a company wants expert support during attacks and refunds for attack-related scaling costs. Which solution?

back.answer: Shield Advanced.
back.explanation: DRT + cost protection is the $3k tier.

cards.front: Ensure WAF rules are applied to all ALBs across 50 accounts, including future accounts. Which solution?

back.answer: Firewall Manager.

choices.why: Rules are per web ACL, not org-wide rollout.

cards.front: Identify S3 buckets containing personally identifiable information. Which service?

back.answer: Macie.

cards.front: Alert when EC2 instances are used for cryptocurrency mining or credentials are compromised. Which service?

back.answer: GuardDuty.

choices.why: Detects threats from logs without agents.

cards.front: Continuously scan EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities (CVEs). Which service?

back.answer: Inspector.
back.explanation: SSM agent on EC2, ECR, Lambda.

choices.why: Scans EC2, ECR, Lambda for CVEs.

cards.front: Single pane of glass for security findings across all accounts and services. Which service?

back.answer: Security Hub.

cards.front: After a GuardDuty finding, analyze and identify the root cause of the incident. Which service?

back.answer: Detective.

choices.why: Graph of relationships reveals root cause.

cards.front: Auditor requests AWS's SOC 2 / PCI compliance reports. Which service?

back.answer: Artifact.

choices.why: Checks your compliance, not AWS's reports.
Self-service download of AWS compliance reports.

cards.front: Keyword: **"SQLi / XSS / HTTP filtering"**

back.answer: WAF

back.answer: WAF rate-based rule

back.answer: WAF Count mode

back.answer: Inspector

back.answer: Security Hub

back.answer: Detective
